# Phase 5 Block-Enum Refactor: Architecture & Migration RFC

**Status:** Draft — awaiting approval before any code lands.
**Author:** generated by the engineering session, 2026-05-23.
**Roadmap reference:** `OOXML_ROADMAP.md` §2 Phase 5, §0.1 decision #2.

## 0. Why this RFC exists

Phases 1-4 carry one assumption end-to-end: the document is a flat
`Vector<Paragraph>`. Tables break that assumption — they are *block-level*
containers whose cells hold their own block sequences (including other
tables). The change is not local to `format-docx`; it cascades into
`engine`, `engine-wasm`, `bridge`, `layout`, `render`, `format-pdf`, and
the TS shell.

This RFC pins the data model, the layout strategy, the rendering
delegation, the bridge / selection / a11y consequences, and a staging
plan that ships in three PRs without a long-lived broken branch.

Per the §0.1 decisions log:
- PDF table export defers to **Phase 5b** (decision #4).
- Strict zero-drift on unmutated paragraphs / tables is mandatory
  (decision #5). Tables ride the same Phase 3 passthrough as paragraphs.
- Ground-truth fixtures author against **Office 365 Web in a Windows VM**;
  LibreOffice Writer is the secondary baseline (decision #1).
- Schema validation against **Part 4 Transitional** XSDs only
  (decision #3).

---

## 1. Data model

### 1.1 The `Block` enum

```rust
// crates/engine/src/lib.rs

pub enum Block {
    Paragraph(Paragraph),
    Table(Table),
}

pub struct DocumentTree {
    /// Top-level block sequence. Previously `Vector<Paragraph>`; now
    /// `Vector<Block>` so a `Table` can appear at any document position.
    /// Still `im::Vector` so undo snapshots clone in O(1).
    pub blocks: Vector<Block>,
}
```

`Block` is the smallest possible enum surface: a table cell's content is
also a `Vec<Block>` (see §1.4), so the same enum carries everything that
can sit inside a `<w:body>` or `<w:tc>`. Future block variants (Phase 7
floating images, Phase 8 footnotes) extend the enum without re-touching
every consumer.

### 1.2 `Table`

```rust
pub struct Table {
    /// `<w:tblGrid>` — column template widths in twips. Length is the
    /// **logical** column count; cells with `grid_span > 1` consume
    /// multiple template columns at render time.
    pub grid: Vec<i32>,

    pub props: TableProperties,
    pub rows: Vec<TableRow>,

    /* Phase 3 passthrough — Tables ride the same byte-stable round-trip
    as paragraphs. The reader captures the `<w:tbl>...</w:tbl>` source
    bytes; the writer emits them verbatim when `!dirty`. */
    pub dirty: bool,
    pub source_xml: Option<Vec<u8>>,
}
```

### 1.3 `TableRow`

```rust
pub struct TableRow {
    pub props: RowProperties,
    pub cells: Vec<TableCell>,
}

pub struct RowProperties {
    /// `<w:trHeight w:val="…" w:hRule="atLeast|exact|auto"/>`
    pub height: Option<RowHeight>,
    /// `<w:cantSplit/>` — row cannot break across pages. Phase 5a
    /// treats this as **implicit-on** for every row (we don't break
    /// rows across pages yet; see §2.3). Carried verbatim for
    /// round-trip.
    pub cant_split: bool,
    /// `<w:tblHeader/>` — row repeats at the top of every page after
    /// a break. Phase 5a captures but does not honour.
    pub header: bool,
}

pub enum RowHeight {
    AtLeast { twips: i32 },
    Exact { twips: i32 },
    Auto,
}
```

`RowProperties` carries everything the writer needs to round-trip; the
layout consumer reads `height` and ignores the rest for Phase 5a.

### 1.4 `TableCell`

```rust
pub struct TableCell {
    pub props: CellProperties,
    /// Nested block sequence. **Recursion lives here** — a `TableCell`
    /// can carry another `Block::Table(...)` for nested tables (which
    /// Word produces routinely for complex layouts). `Vec`, not
    /// `im::Vector`: cells average 1–2 paragraphs, so persistent-
    /// vector overhead is not worth the structural-sharing win for
    /// the typical cell. The top-level `DocumentTree.blocks` keeps
    /// `im::Vector` because undo snapshots clone it whole.
    pub blocks: Vec<Block>,
}

pub struct CellProperties {
    /// `<w:gridSpan w:val="…"/>` — column merge. Default 1.
    pub grid_span: u8,
    /// `<w:vMerge w:val="restart|continue"/>` — vertical merge.
    ///
    /// - `None` — independent cell.
    /// - `Restart` — top of a vertical span; renders its content,
    ///   spans down through any number of `Continue` cells directly
    ///   below.
    /// - `Continue` — placeholder; content is ignored at render
    ///   (the `Restart` cell visually owns the merged block).
    pub v_merge: VMergeRole,
    /// `<w:tcW w:w="…" w:type="dxa|auto|pct|nil"/>` — explicit width.
    /// Overrides the column's `<w:tblGrid>` template width when set.
    pub width: Option<CellWidth>,
    /// `<w:tcBorders>` — per-edge stroke. `None` ⇒ inherit from
    /// `<w:tblBorders>` (TableProperties::borders).
    pub borders: Option<CellBorders>,
    /// `<w:shd>` — background fill colour.
    pub shading: Option<[u8; 4]>,
    /// `<w:vAlign w:val="top|center|bottom"/>` — vertical alignment
    /// of the cell's blocks within the cell's bounding box.
    pub v_align: VerticalAlign,
}

pub enum VMergeRole { None, Restart, Continue }
pub enum CellWidth { Dxa(i32), Pct(u16), Auto, Nil }
pub enum VerticalAlign { Top, Center, Bottom }

pub struct CellBorders {
    pub top: Option<BorderStroke>,
    pub left: Option<BorderStroke>,
    pub bottom: Option<BorderStroke>,
    pub right: Option<BorderStroke>,
    pub inside_h: Option<BorderStroke>,
    pub inside_v: Option<BorderStroke>,
}

pub struct BorderStroke {
    /// `<w:val>` — `single` / `double` / `dotted` / `dashed` / `none`.
    pub style: BorderStyle,
    /// `<w:sz>` — line weight in eighths of a point.
    pub size_eighth_pt: u16,
    pub color: Option<[u8; 4]>,
}
```

### 1.5 `TableProperties`

```rust
pub struct TableProperties {
    /// `<w:tblW>` — total table width. Mirrors `CellWidth`.
    pub width: Option<CellWidth>,
    /// `<w:jc>` — horizontal placement on the page (Start/Center/End).
    pub alignment: Option<Alignment>,
    /// `<w:tblInd>` — indent from leading margin in twips.
    pub indent_twips: i32,
    /// `<w:tblBorders>` — default per-edge stroke for every cell.
    /// Cell-level `CellBorders` override per-edge.
    pub borders: Option<CellBorders>,
    /// `<w:tblCellMar>` — default cell padding (twips, per-edge).
    pub cell_margins: CellMargins,
    /// Phase 6+ paragraph / character / table style inheritance via
    /// `<w:tblStyle w:val="…"/>` — captured but not folded into the
    /// engine at Phase 5a (style cascade for *table* styles is a Phase
    /// 5b follow-up; cell paragraphs already cascade via Phase 3 today).
    pub table_style_id: Option<String>,
}

pub struct CellMargins {
    pub top_twips: i32,
    pub left_twips: i32,
    pub bottom_twips: i32,
    pub right_twips: i32,
}
```

### 1.6 Backwards-compatibility shim during migration

PR 1 lands the enum without breaking every existing consumer. A `DocumentTree`
gets a transitional helper:

```rust
impl DocumentTree {
    /// **Migration shim.** Iterates only the top-level `Block::Paragraph`s,
    /// skipping tables. Phase 5a removes every consumer-side call within
    /// three PRs; the shim is then deleted, not deprecated.
    #[deprecated(note = "use `.blocks` and match on Block; removed end of Phase 5a")]
    pub fn paragraphs(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Paragraph> {
        self.blocks.iter().filter_map(Block::as_paragraph)
    }
}

impl Block {
    pub fn as_paragraph(&self) -> Option<&Paragraph> {
        match self {
            Block::Paragraph(p) => Some(p),
            Block::Table(_) => None,
        }
    }
    pub fn as_paragraph_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut Paragraph> { /* … */ }
    pub fn as_table(&self) -> Option<&Table> { /* … */ }
    pub fn as_table_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut Table> { /* … */ }
}
```

The shim's scope is exactly one PR boundary (PR 1 → PR 3). PR 3 deletes
both `paragraphs()` and the `#[deprecated]` attribute together.

### 1.7 Engine API surface deltas

The current Phase-4 surface that needs rewrites:

| Method | Phase 4 signature | Phase 5a |
|---|---|---|
| `DocumentTree::from_text` | `&str → Self` | unchanged (creates one `Block::Paragraph`) |
| `DocumentTree::from_paragraphs` | `IntoIterator<String>` | unchanged |
| `DocumentTree::from_rich_paragraphs` | `IntoIterator<Paragraph>` | unchanged + new `from_blocks` |
| `DocumentTree::paragraph_count` | `→ u32` | renamed `block_count`; old method via shim returns top-level paragraph count |
| `DocumentTree::paragraph_text(idx)` | `u32 → Option<&str>` | `block_text(BlockPath)` |
| `DocumentTree::insert_text(LogicalPos, …)` | flat `LogicalPos` | takes `BlockPath` (see §4.1) |
| `DocumentTree::set_alignment(start, end, align)` | flat | block-path-aware |
| `DocumentTree::apply_style(…)` | flat | block-path-aware |
| `DocumentTree::delete_range(…)` | flat | block-path-aware |
| `DocumentTree::split_paragraph(LogicalPos)` | flat | block-path-aware, but Tab inside a cell may map to a different command (cell navigation) |
| `Paragraph::*` | (unchanged shape) | unchanged — `Paragraph` itself doesn't grow |

The migration is mostly mechanical: every `LogicalPos { para, offset }`
becomes a `BlockPath` whose final step is a paragraph + offset. Tests
that constructed `LogicalPos { para: 0, offset: 5 }` become
`BlockPath::root_paragraph(0, 5)` via a sugar constructor.

## 2. Layout strategy

### 2.1 New layout boxes

```rust
// crates/layout/src/boxes.rs

/// Top-level page child. `LayoutBlock::Paragraph(b)` is the existing
/// `ParagraphBox`; tables get their own variant.
pub enum LayoutBlock {
    Paragraph(ParagraphBox),
    Table(TableBox),
}

pub struct PageBox {
    pub size: Size,
    pub margins: Margins,
    pub blocks: Vec<LayoutBlock>, // was `Vec<ParagraphBox>`
}

pub struct TableBox {
    pub origin: Point,
    pub size: Size,
    /// Visual borders to stroke around the whole table. Cells emit
    /// their own per-edge borders; `outer` is the perimeter.
    pub outer_borders: CellBorders,
    /// Width of each logical column in device px. `len() == grid.len()`
    /// from `engine::Table::grid`, converted twips → px.
    pub columns: Vec<f32>,
    pub rows: Vec<TableRowBox>,
}

pub struct TableRowBox {
    pub origin: Point,       // relative to TableBox
    pub size: Size,          // width = sum of columns; height = max cell height
    pub cells: Vec<TableCellBox>,
}

pub struct TableCellBox {
    pub origin: Point,       // relative to TableRowBox
    pub size: Size,          // width = sum of spanned columns; height = row height (for the Restart cell of a vMerge run, the cumulative height)
    pub grid_span: u8,
    pub v_merge: VMergeRole,
    pub borders: CellBorders,
    pub shading: Option<[u8; 4]>,
    /// Recursive content — a cell can hold paragraphs *and* nested tables.
    pub content: Vec<LayoutBlock>,
}
```

### 2.2 Column-width algorithm

OOXML's table sizing is famously baroque. Phase 5a ships the
**literal-`<w:tblGrid>`** subset and documents the rest as
known-incomplete:

1. **Phase 5a (this RFC):** column widths come straight from
   `engine::Table::grid` (twips → px). Per-cell `<w:tcW>` overrides
   are *captured* in `CellWidth` but only consulted to validate that
   the cell's declared width matches the grid-implied width; mismatches
   are logged once and the grid wins. `gridSpan` cells take the sum of
   their N spanned column widths.
2. **Phase 5b (PDF cut):** add `CellWidth::Auto` / `Pct` handling
   (Word's `tblLayout` algorithm). Requires a measure pass over cell
   content — out of scope for the engine-state-correct MVP.
3. **Phase 5c:** `<w:tblLayout w:type="autofit"/>` two-pass auto-fit
   (measure → balance → re-layout).

### 2.3 Pagination

Same MVP cut: **rows whole-only.** If a row's measured height exceeds
the remaining content height on the current page, the entire row pushes
to the next page. This is equivalent to `<w:cantSplit/>` being implicit
on for every row. Phase 5a does not honour `<w:tblHeader/>` (header
rows do not repeat on the next page).

Mid-row breaking — splitting a cell's content across two pages — is
deferred to **Phase 5c** because:
- It needs a re-entrant layout pass: lay the cell, measure overflow,
  cut at the deepest splittable point (paragraph break, line break),
  carry the residual into the next page's continuation row.
- It interacts with `<w:cantSplit>` semantics and vertical merging in
  non-obvious ways.
- The existing pagination infrastructure (`engine-wasm::build_page`)
  is single-pass and assumes blocks are atomic vertically.

### 2.4 Per-cell layout recursion

`layout_table` is straightforward when rows are atomic:

1. Build the column widths.
2. For each row:
   a. For each cell, recursively run `layout_block` (a new dispatcher
      that calls `layout_paragraph` or `layout_table` based on the
      `Block` variant) with `max_width = sum(columns[col..col+grid_span])`.
   b. Determine the row height: max of all cell measured heights
      (respecting `vMerge::Continue` cells, which contribute zero
      because the `Restart` cell visually owns them).
   c. Position each cell at the column's leading edge; the `Restart`
      cell of a vMerge run gets a height = sum of the row heights it
      spans.
3. Stack rows top-down at the table origin.

Recursion bound: cells nest tables → cells → tables → … . We cap at
**8 levels** of nesting (matches Word's practical limit) with a
defensive guard in `layout_block`; deeper nesting is treated as a
single-paragraph cell carrying `[nested table omitted]`.

### 2.5 Layout of body text inside cells

Cell paragraphs use the existing Phase 2 indent geometry inside the
cell's bounding box. The cell's content `max_width` is its drawable
width minus left/right `cell_margins`. Phase 3 style cascade,
Phase 4 list markers, Phase 2 indent / spacing / line-height all
work in cells unchanged — they just see a narrower `max_width`.

## 3. Rendering & PDF

### 3.1 Canvas2D + Vello (Phase 5a)

`render::scene::build_display_list` learns the `LayoutBlock` dispatch:

```rust
for block in &page.blocks {
    match block {
        LayoutBlock::Paragraph(p) => paint_paragraph(p, …),
        LayoutBlock::Table(t) => paint_table(t, …),
    }
}
```

`paint_table`:

1. Paint the outer `<w:tblBorders>` rectangle (four `FillRect` strokes).
2. For each row:
   - For each cell (skipping `vMerge::Continue` cells, whose `Restart`
     ancestor owns the visual region):
     - Paint cell shading (`FillRect` behind content).
     - Paint cell content recursively: each `LayoutBlock` inside the
       cell goes through the same `paint_paragraph` / `paint_table`
       dispatcher.
     - Paint cell borders (four `FillRect` strokes — top, right,
       bottom, left). Inside-h / inside-v borders are emitted on the
       cells they bound (the right border of cell `c` and the left
       border of cell `c+1` coincide; we let one win to avoid
       double-stroke — convention: the *first* cell in each pair
       emits, so `right` always wins).

The renderer stays a pure traversal — all geometry comes from
`TableBox` / `TableRowBox` / `TableCellBox` origins + sizes that
`layout_table` baked in. No alignment recomputation, no measure pass.

### 3.2 `format-pdf` — deferred to Phase 5b

Per §0.1 decision #4. The Phase 5a cut:

```rust
// crates/format-pdf/src/lib.rs (Phase 5a)
fn emit_block(block: &LayoutBlock, page: &mut PdfPage, ctx: &mut Ctx) {
    match block {
        LayoutBlock::Paragraph(p) => emit_paragraph(p, page, ctx),
        LayoutBlock::Table(_) => {
            /* Phase 5b — TODO: emit table borders + per-cell content
            via the existing emit_paragraph pipeline. */
            ctx.note_unsupported("table");
        }
    }
}
```

Documents with tables export as PDFs that **omit** the tables (paragraphs
around them export correctly). A warning is recorded in
`PdfExportReport.skipped_blocks`; the UI surfaces it ("PDF export
skipped 2 tables — see Help for details").

Phase 5b plan:
- `TableBox` → PDF graphics: borders via `m`/`l`/`S` path ops, shading
  via `re`/`f`, cell content via `Tj` text-show with offset matrices.
- Page-break handling identical to Phase 5a's "rows whole-only" rule.
- veraPDF/A-1b validation: tables are pure graphics + text, no new
  PDF features required; the existing `format-pdf` PDF/A profile holds.

### 3.3 Visual-diff golden expansion

Phase 5a adds **6 new golden cases** under `tools/visual-diff/golden/`:

- `table_2x2.png` — a 2×2 table with single borders.
- `table_grid_span.png` — a row whose first cell spans 2 columns.
- `table_vmerge.png` — vertical merge of two cells.
- `table_borders_double.png` — `<w:val="double"/>` border style.
- `table_shaded_header.png` — first-row cells with `<w:shd>` fill.
- `table_in_rtl_doc.png` — base-direction RTL; columns reverse.

Per-case tolerance: **2 %** (matches the existing visual-diff farm).

## 4. Blast radius

### 4.1 Bridge `BridgeLogicalPos` → `BlockPath`

The single biggest schema change. Phase 4's flat position:

```rust
// crates/bridge/src/common.rs (Phase 4)
pub struct BridgeLogicalPos {
    pub para: u32,
    pub offset: u32,
}
```

Phase 5a:

```rust
// crates/bridge/src/common.rs (Phase 5a)
pub struct BridgeLogicalPos {
    pub path: BlockPath,
    pub offset: u32,
}

/// Address of a `Block` inside a nested `DocumentTree`. Steps walk
/// from the root `blocks: Vector<Block>` down through table cells.
///
/// Examples:
/// - `BlockPath([Block(7)])` — the 7th top-level paragraph.
/// - `BlockPath([Block(2), Cell { row: 1, col: 0 }, Block(0)])` —
///   the first paragraph of the top-left cell's row 1 of the 3rd
///   top-level block (which must be a `Block::Table`).
pub struct BlockPath {
    pub steps: Vec<PathStep>,
}

pub enum PathStep {
    /// Index into the current `blocks: &[Block]` / `Vec<Block>`.
    Block(u32),
    /// Step from a `Block::Table` into one of its cells.
    Cell { row: u32, col: u32 },
}
```

**Additive at the bridge layer.** The Phase 4 `paragraph` / `offset`
shape becomes `BlockPath::root_paragraph(para, offset)` via a JSON
adapter; the TS shell only changes its position constructor. Every
existing consumer that reads `pos.para` becomes `pos.path` —
straightforward sed-able rename, plus a few hot-path consumers
(hit-test, caret motion, selection bounds) get rewritten to handle the
multi-step path. PR 3 carries this migration.

`LogicalRange` follows the same shape — `start: BlockPath + offset`,
`end: BlockPath + offset`, plus a `RangeKind` enum for the
table-cells-rectangular case (see §4.4).

### 4.2 Engine commands

Phase 4 commands like `Command::InsertText { at: LogicalPos, text }`
keep their shape; only the inner `LogicalPos` widens. **Most engine
commands need no logic change** — `insert_text` walks the path to the
target paragraph, then operates inside it exactly as today.

New commands in PR 3:

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `InsertTable { at, rows, cols }` | Insert empty table at block position. |
| `DeleteTable { path }` | Drop the table at this path. |
| `InsertRow { table_path, after_row }` | New row at index. |
| `DeleteRow { table_path, row }` | Drop row. |
| `InsertColumn { table_path, after_col }` | New column across every row. |
| `DeleteColumn { table_path, col }` | Drop column across every row. |
| `MergeCells { table_path, from: (r, c), to: (r, c) }` | Set `grid_span` / `vMerge` on the top-left, mark covered cells `Continue`. |
| `SplitCell { table_path, row, col }` | Inverse: drop spans. |
| `SetCellShading { table_path, row, col, color }` | `<w:shd>` mutation. |
| `SetCellBorders { table_path, row, col, borders }` | Per-edge stroke. |

Every command flips `Table.dirty = true` and drops `source_xml`, mirroring
the Phase 3 paragraph passthrough invariant.

### 4.3 Accessibility tree

Phase 4's `A11yTree` is a flat list of `A11yParagraph`s. Phase 5a
extends it to a tree:

```rust
// crates/bridge/src/event.rs (Phase 5a)
pub enum A11yNode {
    Paragraph(A11yParagraph),
    Table(A11yTable),
}

pub struct A11yTable {
    /// `role="table"` plus an optional `<caption>` (Phase 6+).
    pub rows: Vec<A11yRow>,
    pub id: u32,
}

pub struct A11yRow {
    pub cells: Vec<A11yCell>,
    pub id: u32,
}

pub struct A11yCell {
    /// `aria-rowspan` / `aria-colspan` from `vMerge` / `gridSpan`.
    pub row_span: u8,
    pub col_span: u8,
    /// Same nested structure: a cell can contain paragraphs and/or
    /// tables. The DOM serialisation emits `<td><p dir>…</p>…</td>`.
    pub nodes: Vec<A11yNode>,
    pub id: u32,
}

pub struct A11yTree {
    pub nodes: Vec<A11yNode>,
}
```

The Phase 4 `AccessibilityTreeDelta` patch shape becomes node-path
addressed:

```rust
pub enum A11yPatch {
    UpdateParagraph { path: BlockPath, para: A11yParagraph },
    UpdateCell { table_path: BlockPath, row: u32, col: u32, cell: A11yCell },
    InsertNode { parent: BlockPath, after: u32, node: A11yNode },
    DeleteNode { path: BlockPath },
    /* PR 3 — full set; PR 2 only emits whole-tree replacement to keep
    scope contained. */
}
```

PR 2 ships **whole-tree** a11y emission for table-bearing documents
(re-emit every node on any table edit). PR 3 lands the fine-grained
patches.

### 4.4 Selection across cells

Word's table selection semantics:

1. **Linear selection inside one cell.** Identical to a paragraph
   selection today. Single `LogicalRange` whose `start.path` and
   `end.path` share a `Cell {row, col}` prefix.
2. **Cell-rectangular selection.** User drags from cell `(r0, c0)` to
   `(r1, c1)` — the selection covers every cell in the rectangle,
   highlighting whole cells rather than text spans. Triggered by
   mouse-down inside a cell + drag into another cell of the same
   table.
3. **Whole-row / whole-column selection.** Triple-click inside a row
   gutter, single-click in column header (Phase 5c).
4. **Mixed: spans into and out of a table.** Anchor inside a
   paragraph, caret inside a cell. Word treats this as a *Linear*
   selection over the entire intervening block range — every cell
   between anchor and caret is fully selected, regardless of where
   the caret actually sits inside the final cell.

Engine schema:

```rust
// crates/engine/src/lib.rs
pub struct Selection {
    pub anchor: BlockPath,
    pub anchor_offset: u32,
    pub caret: BlockPath,
    pub caret_offset: u32,
    pub kind: SelectionKind,
}

pub enum SelectionKind {
    /// Anchor and caret are linear logical positions; the highlight
    /// is contiguous in document order.
    Linear,
    /// Cell-rectangular selection inside a single table. The
    /// rectangle covers every cell whose `(row, col)` is between
    /// `from` and `to` (inclusive). `anchor` / `caret` still point
    /// at character positions inside the corner cells so caret
    /// motion can fall out of cell-rect mode cleanly.
    TableCells {
        table_path: BlockPath,
        from: (u32, u32),
        to: (u32, u32),
    },
}
```

Render-side: `SelectionOverlay` (DOM overlay today) gets a
`TableCellHighlight` mode that paints solid-fill rectangles over each
selected cell instead of per-line text-span rects. The existing
per-line bounding-box infrastructure from Phase 4 is reused for the
*Linear* case — including when the linear range crosses table
boundaries (the in-cell paragraphs each emit their own per-line rects).

### 4.5 Pointer hit-testing

`document_geometry` (`engine-wasm`) currently flattens the box tree
into per-line `CaretSlot`s keyed by paragraph index. Phase 5a:

1. Each `LayoutBlock::Paragraph` keeps its current `CaretSlot`
   emission, but slots are now stamped with the full `BlockPath` to
   their owning paragraph instead of just `para_idx: u32`.
2. Each `LayoutBlock::Table` recursively flattens every cell's
   contents → caret slots stamped with
   `BlockPath([Block(t), Cell {r, c}, Block(b)])`.
3. The hit-test query gains a fast-path: a pointer landing *between*
   cells (in border / gutter space) snaps to the nearest cell's
   leading caret position — never to "outside the table" once a
   cell has been entered, because Word users expect pointer-in-table
   == caret-in-table.

PR 2 ships paragraph-only hit-testing inside tables (sufficient for
"click to position caret inside a cell"). PR 3 ships the
cell-rectangular selection drag.

### 4.6 Undo

`UndoStack` stores `DocumentTree` snapshots. With `blocks:
Vector<Block>`, cloning a snapshot is still O(1); the only growth is
that mutated tables clone their `rows: Vec<TableRow>` (which is not
`im::Vector`). Per-snapshot cost stays bounded — depth-100 cap holds.

The perf harness adds an undo/redo p95 test against a 50-table doc
to catch any regression.

### 4.7 `format-docx::writer` passthrough extension

The Phase 3 paragraph passthrough optimisation extends naturally:

```rust
fn emit_block(block: &Block, out: &mut String) {
    match block {
        Block::Paragraph(p) => emit_paragraph(p, out),
        Block::Table(t) => emit_table(t, out),
    }
}

fn emit_table(t: &Table, out: &mut String) {
    if !t.dirty && let Some(raw) = &t.source_xml {
        out.push_str(std::str::from_utf8(raw).unwrap_or(""));
    } else {
        regenerate_table(t, out);
    }
}
```

A **whole-table** mutation (`InsertRow`, `DeleteCell`, etc.) flips
`Table.dirty = true` and drops `Table.source_xml`. **Cell-content
mutations** (typing inside a cell) flip *both* the inner paragraph's
`dirty` flag *and* the containing `Table.dirty`. The latter is
mandatory: if a cell paragraph regenerates while the surrounding
`<w:tbl>` is emitted verbatim, the writer mixes original `<w:tr>`
bytes with regenerated `<w:p>` bytes and produces invalid XML.

This implies: **editing a single paragraph in a 200-row table
regenerates the whole table on save.** Phase 5a accepts that cost
(the alternative is per-row passthrough, which is a Phase 5c
follow-up). Phase 5a documents the trade-off in `docx.md`.

### 4.8 TS shell impact

Migration carries through `EngineClient` → React/Solid components:

| Component | Change |
|---|---|
| `EditorCanvas` | unchanged — still owns one `<canvas>`. |
| `HiddenInput` | unchanged — `beforeinput` semantics identical inside cells. |
| `CaretOverlay` | path-aware: caret position now arrives as a `BlockPath`. |
| `SelectionOverlay` | adds `kind == TableCells` rendering — solid cell-fill highlights. |
| `AccessibilityTree` | tree-aware DOM: nested `<table><tr><td>` structure. |
| Toolbar (new) | "Insert Table" button + table-context controls (add row, merge cells). PR 3 deliverable. |
| Keyboard | `Tab` inside cell → next cell; `Shift+Tab` → prev; arrow keys cross cell boundaries when caret is at cell edge. |

### 4.9 Bridge schema bump

The bridge schema has grown additively for four phases. Phase 5a's
`BlockPath` adds a new tagged enum and three new commands per §4.2.
**Additive only** — every Phase 4 command keeps working through the
JSON `BridgeLogicalPos` shape, which serialises as
`{ path: [{ kind: "Block", idx: N }], offset: M }`. The TS shell's
old `{ para: N, offset: M }` shape is rejected by the parser; the TS
constructor switches in lock-step with PR 3.

---

## 5. Execution staging — three PRs

Phase 5a ships in three sequential PRs, each landing on `main` with
green CI. Each PR's working branch is rebased on `main` daily — no
long-lived integration branch.

### PR 1 — Engine data model + opaque table parse (≈ 1.5 weeks)

**Goal:** the `Block` enum exists; tables parse as opaque source-XML
blobs (no rows / cells modelled yet); every existing consumer still
compiles via the `paragraphs()` shim.

Deliverables:
- `engine::Block`, `Table`, `TableRow`, `TableCell`, all property
  structs from §1. Empty `Vec<TableRow>` is valid.
- `DocumentTree.blocks: Vector<Block>` (was `paragraphs`).
- `paragraphs()` migration shim per §1.6.
- `format-docx::parts::document` parses `<w:tbl>...</w:tbl>` as a
  whole and stores it as a `Block::Table` with `rows: vec![]`,
  `source_xml: Some(raw_bytes)`, `dirty: false`. The captured bytes
  ride the Phase 3 passthrough — round-trip is byte-stable.
- Writer's `emit_block` dispatch — `Block::Table` always passthrough
  (no `regenerate_table` yet).
- A new fixture `table_2x2_opaque.docx` round-trips with drift = 0.
- Layout: `LayoutBlock::Table` variant exists, but `layout_block` for
  a `Table` emits a placeholder paragraph "[table]" at the table's
  position so existing renderers + perf harness keep working.
- A11y: tables emit a single `<p>[table]</p>` placeholder node.
- Every Phase 1-4 fixture stays green.

CI gates: all pre-existing gates green; one new fixture
(`table_2x2_opaque.docx`) green.

Risk: low. Pure additive enum + writer passthrough are well-understood
from Phase 3.

### PR 2 — Row / cell parse + layout + Canvas render (≈ 3 weeks)

**Goal:** Tables render correctly on screen. PDF export skips them.

Deliverables:
- `format-docx::parts::document` extends to `<w:tr>` and `<w:tc>` with
  `<w:tcPr>` (gridSpan, vMerge, tcW, tcBorders, shd, vAlign) and
  `<w:trPr>` (trHeight, cantSplit, tblHeader).
- `engine::TableRow.cells` + `TableCell.blocks` populated; nested
  tables work end-to-end.
- `layout::TableBox` + `TableRowBox` + `TableCellBox` per §2.1.
  Literal `<w:tblGrid>` column widths; rows whole-only pagination.
- Canvas2D + Vello: `paint_table` per §3.1.
- `format-pdf`: stub per §3.2. PDF export of table-bearing docs emits
  a warning in `PdfExportReport`.
- New `table_2x2.docx` (no passthrough, fully regenerated emit) round-
  trips with drift ≤ 50 B (small attribute-order shuffle is OK; Phase
  3 passthrough is the byte-stable path, regenerate path has a
  loose bound).
- Visual-diff goldens for §3.3.
- A11y: whole-tree emission per §4.3 (no fine-grained patches yet).
- Pointer hit-testing inside cells.

CI gates: all pre-existing + 6 new visual-diff goldens green at 2 %
tolerance.

Risk: high. Layout + render of tables is the meatiest engineering item
in the whole roadmap. Mitigations:
- `paint_table` is feature-flagged behind `RENDER_TABLES=true` (off by
  default) for the first half of PR 2; goldens activate the flag.
- The PR is reviewed in two halves — parser + engine model first, then
  layout + render.

### PR 3 — Bridge commands + UI + fine-grained a11y (≈ 3 weeks)

**Goal:** users can insert tables, edit cells, navigate with Tab, see
selection across cells, and screen-reader users get proper
`<table>/<tr>/<td>` semantics.

Deliverables:
- `bridge::BlockPath` per §4.1 (additive enum variants, JSON-tagged).
- Engine commands per §4.2: insert/delete table/row/column,
  merge/split cells, set shading/borders.
- TS shell: "Insert Table" toolbar button + table-context menu.
- Cell-rectangular selection per §4.4 (`SelectionKind::TableCells`).
- Tab / Shift-Tab cell navigation.
- Fine-grained a11y patches per §4.3.
- Migration shim `paragraphs()` removed.
- New fixtures: `table_grid_span.docx`, `table_vmerge.docx`,
  `table_nested.docx`, `table_in_rtl_doc.docx`.
- Manual Word-opens-without-repair sign-off per §3.5.

CI gates: all pre-existing + 4 new round-trip fixtures + all 6
visual-diff goldens still green + Playwright e2e: "Insert Table",
"Tab navigates cells", "Cell selection drag", "Type into cell — save
and re-open — text preserved".

Risk: medium-high. Bridge schema change touches every existing TS
position consumer, but each consumer change is mechanical (one extra
hop in the JSON shape).

### Phase 5b (separate cut, ≈ 1-2 weeks)

PR 4 deliverables:
- `format-pdf::emit_table` per §3.2 design.
- veraPDF/A-1b validation against `table_2x2.docx`,
  `table_borders_double.docx`, `table_in_rtl_doc.docx`.
- New `tools/pdf-validate/tables/` harness.

Risk: low — pure additive `format-pdf` work.

### Phase 5c (deferred)

- Row-break across pages (true mid-row pagination).
- `<w:tblHeader/>` repeating headers.
- `<w:cantSplit/>` honoured per-row.
- Per-row passthrough (cell-content mutation doesn't dirty the
  whole table).
- `CellWidth::Auto` / `Pct` auto-fit (Word's `tblLayout`).
- Whole-row / whole-column triple-click selection.

Phase 5c is *not* on the critical path to "tables ship to users";
it's the polish pass.

---

## 6. Decisions to confirm before PR 1 kicks off

1. **`Vec<Block>` vs `Vector<Block>` in `TableCell.blocks`.** RFC
   recommends `Vec`. Confirm — switching later requires a
   touch-everything refactor.
2. **Migration shim deletion timing.** RFC schedules removal in PR 3.
   If we want shipping `v0.6.0-beta.X` on PR 1 + PR 2 (table-display
   but not table-edit), the shim stays through one extra beta cut.
3. **Cell-edit dirties the whole table?** §4.7. RFC accepts the cost
   for Phase 5a; per-row passthrough is Phase 5c. Confirm we're OK
   with regenerate-on-cell-edit (a 200-row table edit regenerates
   ~200 KB of XML).
4. **Phase 5b vs 5c cut on PDF.** RFC defers PDF tables to 5b *only*
   (Phase 5a ships without). Confirm that's still the call vs.
   pushing PDF further to 5c.
5. **PR 1 placeholder "[table]" rendering.** Acceptable to ship
   intermediate `main` revisions where tables visually omit? PR 2
   restores correct rendering ~3 weeks later. Alternative: feature-
   flag the whole Block enum until PR 2 lands.

Recommended answers, in order: yes / yes (PR 3) / yes / yes / yes.

---

## 7. Test plan

The §3 visual-diff goldens are the smoke test. The semantic round-trip
fixtures from PR 1-3 are the byte-stability gate. Additional unit
tests carry on the Phase 1-4 pattern: literal-XML test snippets in
`crates/format-docx/src/parts/document.rs` for `<w:tbl>` / `<w:tr>`
/ `<w:tc>` parsing edge cases (gridSpan + vMerge interaction, missing
`<w:tcPr>`, nested tables).

Specifically required new tests per phase:

| PR | Tests |
|---|---|
| PR 1 | `Block::Table opaque parses with row vec empty`; `table passthrough byte-identical`; `engine block_count counts tables`. |
| PR 2 | `tcPr parses gridSpan + vMerge`; `column widths from tblGrid`; `cell layout recurses to nested table`; `pagination pushes overflow row to next page`; `Canvas paint emits border + shading commands`. |
| PR 3 | `BlockPath round-trips through bridge JSON`; `InsertTable command appears at correct position`; `MergeCells flips Continue cells`; `TableCells selection covers rectangle`. |

A new fuzz target `fuzz/table_parser` joins the suite in PR 2 — random
`<w:tbl>` element shapes go through `parse_document_xml` and assert
no panic.

---

## 8. Open questions for the human reviewer

1. **Per-row passthrough.** §4.7 trade-off. Acceptable for MVP?
2. **Vec vs im::Vector for cell content.** §1.4. Default `Vec`.
3. **Migration shim lifetime.** §1.6. End of PR 3.
4. **Tab inside a cell** — by default takes you to the next cell. Do
   we want a modifier to insert a literal tab character inside a cell
   (Word: Ctrl+Tab)? Default yes, mirror Word.
5. **Selection drag-out-of-cell semantics.** Anchor in a cell, caret
   drags out of the table — Word switches to *Linear* selection and
   the cell becomes fully-selected (every character inside it). Match
   exactly?

## 9. Definition of "Phase 5a done"

Sign-off requires **all** of:

- [ ] PRs 1, 2, 3 merged to `main` with green CI.
- [ ] 4 new round-trip fixtures (`table_2x2`, `table_grid_span`,
      `table_vmerge`, `table_nested`, `table_in_rtl_doc`) all green
      with drift = 0 on the passthrough path.
- [ ] 6 new visual-diff goldens green at 2 % tolerance.
- [ ] At least one real Office-365-Web-authored 5-page document with
      tables opens, edits, saves, re-opens in Word without a repair
      dialog.
- [ ] Insert-latency p95 stays under the §6 perf budget on a doc
      containing a 50-row table.
- [ ] WASM artifact under 15 MiB.
- [ ] Playwright e2e: "Insert 3×3 table → type in 4 cells → save →
      reload → text preserved" passes.
- [ ] `OOXML_ROADMAP.md` §0.1 + §1.3 passthrough table updated to
      reflect Phase 5a state.

Phase 5b sign-off: PDF tables export + veraPDF validation green
on the same 5 fixtures.

Phase 5c sign-off: tracked separately; not blocking the `v0.7.0`
beta cut.
